data.narrative:
eleQtron, a Series A quantum computing company founded by Christof Wunderlich, Michael Johanning, and Jan Henrik Leisse, has raised €50M+ to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public comps (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

A Stage-Progression valuation method is applicable here, using the €50M total raised as a proxy base value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement. This yields an implied valuation of €100M. A Peer-Median approach was not feasible; while 8 same-sector private companies exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3 required), and using an all-sector median would risk misrepresentation.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of €85M to €115M, with a median of €100M. This range reflects the single applicable method and carries meaningful uncertainty around stage-specific multiples and the early-stage nature of quantum computing as an asset class. Key risks to valuation include technology development velocity, path to commercialization clarity, and the nascent public-market reference points available for calibration. Additional data on cash burn, technical milestones, and customer traction would narrow this band considerably.
